content.title: About
content.content: Hard plain salted pretzels are a baked snack made from wheat flour, water, yeast and salt, shaped into the iconic twisted knot and baked until crisp. They have a mildly salty, slightly sweet flavor and a crunchy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pretzels have ancient origins, with ancestors dating back to medieval Europe.
They are traditionally associated with Bavarian beer culture and are often served with beer.
The knot shape symbolized crossed arms, a medieval German sign of blessing.
Hard salted pretzels are usually sprinkled with coarse sea salt, enhancing their taste.
In the 19th century United States, pretzels became a popular street snack.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Hard pretzels provide a quick source of energy thanks to their high complex carbohydrate content.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many snack foods, they contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: The wheat flour used supplies modest amounts of iron, which supports blood formation.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 aids protein metabolism and supports the nervous system.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The added salt helps maintain electrolyte balance, though intake should be monitored.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: The amount of salt can raise blood pressure in salt‑sensitive individuals.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Pretzels contain wheat, so they are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While low in fat, the carbohydrate content makes them fairly calorie‑dense if eaten in large portions.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to wheat flour.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels are convenient as a standalone snack, paired with cheese, mustard, hummus, or added to salads. A quick warm‑up in the oven restores extra crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent moisture absorption and loss of crispness.
